question: A 4-year-old has bloody diarrhoea for 5 days, is anuric, has Hb 6.8 g/dL with fragmented red cells on blood film, and platelets 48,000/µL. His serum creatinine is markedly elevated. Which action is CONTRAINDICATED in this child?

answers.text: Peritoneal dialysis to manage uraemia and fluid overload

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dialysis is the appropriate management for severe AKI with uraemia, hyperkalaemia, or refractory fluid overload in HUS — this is NOT contraindicated.

Correct. Antibiotics — particularly trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole — are CONTRAINDICATED in EHEC (O157:H7)-associated HUS. They induce bacterial lysis with massive Shiga toxin release, worsening endothelial injury and the HUS triad. This is a high-yield PE known-trap.

answers.text: Careful fluid resuscitation to correct prerenal component

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Judicious fluid resuscitation is appropriate in HUS to manage the prerenal component before anuria is fully established; this is not contraindicated.

answers.text: Packed red cell transfusion for haemoglobin below 6 g/dL

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Transfusion for severe anaemia in HUS is appropriate and not contraindicated; microangiopathic haemolysis may require transfusion.

overallFeedback.feedback: In EHEC-associated HUS (the triad: microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia + thrombocytopenia + AKI after bloody diarrhoea), antibiotics are CONTRAINDICATED because they lyse bacteria and release Shiga toxin in bulk, worsening endothelial and renal injury.
Antibiotics (especially TMP-SMX) are absolutely contraindicated in EHEC-HUS — they trigger Shiga toxin release and worsen the syndrome.
